name: Set organic account and platform strategy
what: Decide which platforms the brand runs organically, set account positioning and content pillars, and keep the visual world and account setup consistent and compliant across platforms.
encompasses: Write a positioning statement and test it against a competitor swap
Split unrelated product lines into separate accounts when needed
Pick 2 to 3 content pillars mapped to products or collections
Pick 1 hero platform from where buyers actually spend time
Treat secondary platforms as free reach with no sales expectation
Set account type (Creator vs Business) and register from the selling country
Keep the product's visual world consistent across every platform
Adapt a proven concept's length and cut per platform, same core idea
Flag a case for funding an owned media property instead of another promotion round
founder_sees: Which platforms we run, the account setup, and the positioning line, for approval before anything is created.

name: Build the content pillar calendar and cadence plan
what: Turn the pillars into a postable calendar: set a posting floor the team can hold, sequence SKUs and stock-status moments, and give the plan a fair test window before judging it.
encompasses: Set starting cadence by catalogue shape (hero SKU vs wide catalogue)
Set a weekly posting floor the team can hold for 4 weeks straight
Rotate which SKU gets a post so no item goes untouched for a month
Confirm stock, shipping and reply capacity before a post is built to pull orders
Turn stock status into content: restocks, low-stock framing, waitlists
Post a reorder reminder for consumable or replenishable products
Track posts shipped against the floor as the only KPI in months 1 to 3
Hold the pillar mix 3 months and give the channel 12 months before a verdict
Test a scheduler against manual posting only after 4 weeks manual
Do not abandon the account after a run of weak posts
inputs: brand brain: stock and shipping status
idea bank (this agent's own story bank)
founder_sees: This week's and this month's posting plan, tied to real stock and shipping status.

name: Plan founder-on-camera participation
what: Decide how much the founder appears on camera, on which account, and build fast-turnaround formats for when the founder is the only person who can film that day.
encompasses: Choose expert-vs-student on-camera stance based on what the brand can prove
Put founder personality on the founder's own account, not the brand handle
Diagnose a sales plateau as a founder-capacity ceiling before blaming the product
Build a creator bench and shared footage archive before the founder becomes the ceiling
Publish small posts to find the founder's voice instead of waiting to feel ready
Build a 30-minute founder-history carousel for a same-day calendar gap
Balance proof-led positioning with founder personality for considered purchases
inputs: brand brain: founder bio and story bank
founder_sees: A plan for how much time the founder needs on camera, and a warning when the founder is the growth bottleneck.

name: Write short-video scripts, hooks and captions
what: Write the actual hook lines, scripts and captions for organic video and image posts, one named SKU and one named buyer per post, matched to the brand voice and reading level.
encompasses: Spend most hook-planning time on the first 3 seconds and the first frame
Pick a hook type on purpose from a fixed menu and log it
Write every caption to one named customer, in the buyer's own words
Cap reading level below tenth grade and cut jargon, adverbs and stacked synonyms
Open dry product topics with the scene the buyer already cares about
Give every story-led video a real ending: reveal, fix or offer
Write comparison posts to a real, one-sentence verdict
Answer the questions buyers are embarrassed to ask
Turn shipping and returns policy clarity into pre-purchase trust content
Test warning-style vs benefit-style hooks on the same product
Run every script through a pre-publish quality checklist
Warm up with short copywork and leave an incubation gap before editing high-stakes copy
inputs: brand brain: voice (liked and disliked examples)
founder_sees: Draft scripts and captions ready to film or post, each tied to a SKU and a claim the brand record backs.

name: Design repeatable formats and series
what: Turn a winning one-off post into a named, repeatable series or format the team can run without the founder, including a citation-worthy video format when it also serves answer-engine visibility.
encompasses: Turn a winning format into a named, repeatable series with a signature
Put most new-account effort into product demo formats over Stories
Turn a repeatable demo into a safe, genuine challenge series
Prefer formats a team can repeat many times a day without the founder
Run the carousel/design path when nobody will go on camera
Run a winning format for at least 8 weeks while a second format stays live
Produce a search-hit video and its companion page for a cited category term
founder_sees: A named, repeatable format the team can run on its own, with the cadence to test it fairly.

name: Plan production batching and shoot setup
what: Set the practical shoot logistics: fixed batching days, a simple lighting setup, and when to raise production stakes with a location change.
encompasses: Batch scripting and filming on separate fixed days
Set up 1 key light and practical background lights for every shoot
Raise production stakes with a location change when talking-head content goes flat
founder_sees: A shoot schedule that fits the team's real time, with a simple gear list.

name: Maintain the idea bank, story mining and competitive teardown
what: Keep a running supply of postable ideas by mining comments, product facts and founder stories, and by tearing down competitor and category videos for structure only, never content.
encompasses: Keep a permanent bank of 10 to 20 one-line post ideas naming a SKU
Turn the questions under best posts into new posts from month 2
Turn a proven category post into a new one with the store's own angle
Build the story set: founder history, sourcing trips, failed batches, positions
Mine product stories with a fixed question set when the idea bank runs low
Keep categorised swipe files split by DTC competitor vs non-retail sources
Tear down a winning video with a beginning-middle-end grid
Do first competitive-format research by hand with 3 buyer phrases
Filter story topics with a 60-second voice-memo test
Reverse-engineer top niche videos with AI before remaking the brand's own
Never paste swiped structure as if it were the brand's own copy
inputs: brand brain: product facts and founder history
founder_sees: A running list of ready post ideas, and a note on what a competitor's structure teaches us, never their words.

name: Run AI-assisted drafting with a mandatory human gate
what: Use AI only to remix approved lines, organize research or draft a first pass; a human always originates the story, fact-checks the draft and rewrites before anything publishes.
encompasses: Let humans originate stories and positions; use AI only to remix approved lines
Keep a positions log of the brand's side on category debates
Use AI as a pre-publish reviewer with targeted questions, not an open prompt
Check every AI-remixed piece for facts and voice before it goes live
Ask monthly whether an AI-drafted piece added something new or only rearranged
Ground every AI-assisted draft in the real catalog feed and existing reviews
Run every AI-assisted draft through outline approval, fact-check and a human rewrite pass
Build a reusable brand-voice reference file for AI prompts
Keep one persistent AI workspace holding the brand brief and research exports
Draft with AI, add first-hand detail, edit by hand, never bulk-publish
Keep a human-approval gate in every automated content pipeline
Package a repeated procedure into one reviewed, repeatable pipeline
inputs: brand brain: voice and claims tiers
founder_sees: Nothing directly; this is the internal check that stops an ungrounded AI draft from ever reaching the founder or the site.

name: Draft comment and DM community responses
what: Draft fast, specific replies to comments and DMs with a real next step, and check that any DM automation stays inside current platform policy.
encompasses: Answer every comment and DM fast with a specific reply and a next step
Send a thank-you-only DM on a new follow, with no pitch or code
Follow up in DM with buyers who clicked the link but did not order
Test the DM funnel end to end before any triggering post goes live
Run DM automation only inside current platform policy with an approved partner
outputs: draft replies for a human to send
founder_sees: Draft replies queued for a person to review and send; a warning if DM automation drifts from platform policy.

name: Design the comment-to-DM and lead-magnet funnel
what: Design how a post turns a stranger into an owned contact: comment-keyword-to-DM flows, lead magnets that match what the buyer actually wants, and routing viral spikes into the funnel instead of a hard pitch.
encompasses: Replace 'link in bio' with a comment keyword that DMs the buyer directly
Use 1 distinct keyword per campaign or SKU for clean attribution
Attach a lead magnet to only 1 or 2 posts a week
Match the lead magnet to something the buyer actually wants
Set a launch cadence of continuous lead magnets plus 1 to 2 launches a year
Route every CTA to owned destinations, never to another social platform
Build the brand's own list from organic reach instead of relying on sponsorships
Route viral spikes to the mid-funnel asset, never straight to a hard pitch
inputs: brand brain: offers and lead magnets
founder_sees: A funnel design (keyword, DM, lead magnet) for approval before it goes live.

name: Repurpose UGC and reviews into content
what: Turn verified customer reviews, photos and unboxing moments into postable content.
encompasses: Turn verified reviews and customer photos into posts
Film or source the unboxing or packaging reveal as its own format
Check UGC and review consent and credit before adding it to the content library
founder_sees: Ready-to-post content built from real customer reviews and photos.

name: Route content to a live, matching commerce destination
what: Confirm every post's next step lands on a live, matching page or Story tag before it publishes, and tag each post by funnel stage for later reuse.
encompasses: Tag every post top, mid or bottom funnel and plan its reuse
Move restocks, codes and CTAs to Stories once followers exist
Use native shoppable tags on Instagram and Facebook, not only TikTok Shop
Set the CTA-free window and view threshold by the store's price point
Send every post's next step to a live, matching PDP or landing page
Offer a bundle or higher-tier product in CTA content, not only the entry item
Confirm link, stock and price are ready before a high-performing post publishes
Pick 1 hero SKU per post instead of a generic 'our products' post
founder_sees: A pass/fail check that every post's link, stock and price are real before it goes out.

name: Reuse and retire content across surfaces
what: Track each asset's shelf life and reuse it across the PDP, email, DM, post-purchase flow and other owned channels before retiring it on schedule.
encompasses: Label every post timely or timeless and strip dates from reusable content
Reuse every content asset across the PDP, email, DM and post-purchase surfaces
Reuse a sales-moving post at least 4 times with a changed wrapper
Reuse a story across brand-controlled accounts only, with a different wrapper
Feed one deep piece into many store surfaces
Mark a well-told story approved and reuse the exact line
Only commission a content library with a distribution plan already in place
Retire launch and sale posts after their window; never resurface a dated post
Repost a timeless post again once it passes 60 days old
Repurpose the blog's RSS feed into cross-channel social posts
Repeat proven category queries as content across every owned channel
Amplify an on-site article on the company's own social account
founder_sees: A weekly list of what to reuse where, and what to retire.

name: Run organic creator and UGC-creator seeding
what: Source and manage organic (unpaid or product-only) creator seeding: gifting, sampling and UGC creator briefs that feed the content library, distinct from any paid influencer deal.
encompasses: Build a creator brief from the content pillars and voice guide
Source creators through seeding or UGC-creator platforms for product-only exchange
Track seeded product against content actually delivered
Screen creator content for claims and voice before adding it to the library
Feed approved creator content into the reuse pipeline (ORG-C13)
founder_sees: A seeding plan (who, what product, what's expected back) for approval before any product goes out.

name: Run the organic content claims and safety gate
what: Check every organic post against the brand record's claims tiers and a fixed risk checklist before it can publish: numbers, authority claims, controversy, safety and disclosure.
encompasses: Use only specific product numbers the brand record can back
Only cite a named, real lab, standard or body in authority claims
Sharpen flat copy with the most charged true wording, never exaggeration
Name a shipping delay or bad batch directly and own it, with no spin
Check every number and claim against the brand record before publishing
Treat competitor and creator content as structure only, never copy the content
Route every controversial or comparative claim through legal review first
Screen any post naming real people or news for defamation or endorsement risk
Never run a dangerous stunt for a hook or a challenge
Run a disclosure check before publishing any AI voice or synthetic footage
Test raw or edgy content on a lower-stakes account for luxury or regulated brands
Never paste swiped wording into a caption, PDP or ad
inputs: brand brain: claims tiers (approved, site-backed, forbidden)
outputs: claims-pass or claims-fail verdict with reason
founder_sees: A pass or fail on every post's claims, with the reason for any fail.

name: Read and report organic content performance
what: Read organic performance at the SKU and hook level, watch for stranger-blind content and broad low-value hits, and produce the monthly read against the store's own baseline, never an outside benchmark.
encompasses: Flag a broad viral hit with no buyer signal as a warning, not a win, and check the next 3 posts after it for on-target reach
Read retention, 3-second watch rate and completion/saves/comments/replays per SKU, not raw views
Flag stranger-blind content when follower share of views tops 70 to 80%, and audit the last 20 videos for topic and buyer consistency
Tie content to sales with simple checks computed in code, and track leads per post and which keywords convert to orders
Set the store's own engagement baseline instead of chasing an outside number
Build 3 top-post lists plus a flop list, each showing the SKU featured
Track hook type against post performance and SKU over time, and judge a format over weeks and several SKUs, never by 1 post
Use a content-only discount code as a simple attribution signal
Run the generate-test-measure-scale loop on one strong idea, using next-day recall as a tiebreaker between concepts
inputs: brand brain: past posts and SKUs
founder_sees: A monthly report: what worked, what flopped, and whether the account is reaching real strangers or only existing followers.

name: Set the SEO and AEO work roadmap and priorities
what: Decide whether and where to spend SEO or AEO effort at all: check category demand and margin first, sequence the work (technical floor, then money pages, then one cluster, then links), and set founder expectations before anything starts.
encompasses: Check category search demand and margin before starting any SEO work
Never tie a launch or promotion date to an unranked SEO page
Fix the technical floor, then money pages, then one content cluster, then links
Concentrate content and link work on one category per quarter
Benchmark only against competitors that outrank you for shared terms, and protect position 1 for the brand's own name
Do traditional SEO ranking work before any AI answer-engine visibility work
Keep the SEO budget intact and add AI-search spend on top of it, not instead
Choose 1 to 3 AI platforms to prioritize from where buyers actually research
Screen every AEO tactic by time horizon and real shopper benefit before adopting it
Split AEO ownership between the page owner and a community-content owner
Follow a fixed 30-day and 90-day sequence when starting or restarting SEO
Consider a focused-competitor structural response as a founder-level flag, not our own call
founder_sees: A recommended order of work and budget split between SEO and AEO, with the reason, before spend starts.

name: Research keywords, buyer questions and page briefs
what: Build and maintain the keyword and buyer-question map the whole content program runs from, then turn each target into a structured page brief before any page is written.
encompasses: Score every candidate keyword on demand, fit, intent and difficulty, mining free sources before paying for a tool
Hand-sweep every keyword export to remove irrelevant and competitor-brand terms
Build a topical map with cluster, page type and status columns
Run a keyword gap analysis against real SEO competitors
Classify every target keyword by intent and match it to the right page type
Only target a top-of-funnel keyword when a conversion path exists behind it
Re-run keyword research after any catalog change and on a fixed schedule
Mine People Also Ask, Search Console questions and Reddit for buyer phrasing
Build the buyer-question list from the catalog first, then mine keywords
Pull tail questions from support tickets, sales calls and live chat
Read the top 5 ranking pages and note what a shopper needs that they skip
Write a structured page brief (keyword, intent, format, outline) before production
inputs: web pass: keyword and question sources
founder_sees: The list of terms and buyer questions we can win, and a brief for each page before it gets written.

name: Plan site architecture, URLs and navigation
what: Design how the catalog maps to pages: the collection tree, URL types, subcollections, menu structure and multi-region or multi-language pages, and cap doorway-page risk.
encompasses: Draw the full site architecture tree before building or restructuring the catalog
Assign collection, product and homepage URLs by query breadth
Give real collection pages to any filter combination with its own demand
Split a collection into subcollections only when each has its own demand
Fix keyword cannibalization by giving every topic exactly 1 page
Scale the main menu to the catalog and feature high-volume collections on the homepage
Keep URLs short and keyword-bearing; 301-redirect every URL change
Cap and justify any templated set of near-duplicate pages before scaling it
Build region-specific or hreflang pages for a store selling into more than 1 country
Host FAQ, care and policy pages in a subdirectory, not an isolated subdomain
Map the catalog to exactly one page per distinct product and useful collection
outputs: developer brief for a Shopify/custom theme
founder_sees: A map of how the catalog should be organized into pages and menus, as a developer-ready plan.

name: Run the technical SEO and AI-crawlability audit
what: Crawl the whole site (mobile and JavaScript rendering) to find and fix the technical floor: indexing, canonicals, sitemap, robots.txt, redirects, heading structure and AI-crawler access, and hand off anything that is really a speed fix.
encompasses: Fix the 4-item technical floor before chasing any other SEO work
Crawl the whole site with mobile and JavaScript rendering; fix errors first, using the URL Inspection reason before acting on any not-indexed page
Fix canonical tags, the sitemap and robots.txt so each is correct without blocking a wanted page or an AI crawler
301-redirect every dead URL, including made-up AI-referred ones, to its nearest relevant page
Fix heading structure to exactly 1 H1 per page, and put money-page/FAQ content in the initial server HTML (test with JavaScript off)
Fix Shopify's duplicate product URLs, utility pages, variant duplication and stale app metafields
Check robots.txt and CDN AI-bot settings for crawler blocks on day 1 and after every platform change, testing access with a spoofed bot fetch
Decide and document a bot access policy: allow search and citation bots, decide on training bots, keep checkout blocked
Treat mobile as the primary storefront technical target, not a speed footnote
Verify any AI-applied technical change on the live rendered page, not a summary
Log the store's own speed baseline and run a quick image/app speed triage before escalating to Site
outputs: developer brief for Site specialist on speed items

external_write.surface: robots.txt / sitemap / theme code / CDN settings

founder_sees: The list of technical errors found, in fix order, and confirmation once each is live.

name: Optimize product page SEO
what: Write and structure product-page content so it ranks and reads well: real titles, a full fact-based content stack, image SEO, and dedicated templates for subscriptions and bundles.
encompasses: Index a product page only when its name or attributes have real search volume
Rewrite product titles the way a shopper actually searches; use the title as the H1
Build the full product content stack with explicit facts, not manufacturer copy
Fix product image SEO: descriptive names, real alt text, compression, lazy-load rules
Add first-hand experience signals to product and comparison pages
Use only real product photos on product pages; save stock or generated images for blog posts
Build a dedicated page template for subscription products (cadence, pause, price-per-delivery)
Give every bundle or kit its own product page with its own keyword and spec table
Put subscription plan terms and cancellation policy in the same fact blocks as price
Cap the FAQ at 5 questions on a product page
outputs: product page copy and structure spec
founder_sees: Rewritten product page copy and structure, ready for the site.

name: Optimize collection page SEO
what: Write and structure collection pages so they carry both ranking content and a real buying-decision aid: title, description, grid rules, FAQ and reviews.
encompasses: Set the collection title tag, H1 and URL to the target keyword
Add a real description above and below the collection grid, not a bare grid
Fix the collection grid to 36 to 48 products, numbered pagination, no JS-only rendering
Add a real FAQ accordion and genuine featured reviews to collection pages
Rewrite search engine listings (meta title and description) for clicks, not just keywords
outputs: collection page copy and structure spec
founder_sees: Rewritten collection page copy and layout spec, ready for the site.

name: Implement and validate structured data
what: Add and validate Product, Review, FAQ, Breadcrumb and Offer schema on every money page, deploying through Google Tag Manager when there is no direct theme access.
encompasses: Collect unincentivised post-purchase reviews and emit Review and AggregateRating schema
Implement and validate Product, Review, FAQ and Breadcrumb schema on every money page
Deploy schema markup through Google Tag Manager when theme code access is unavailable
Keep Product, Offer and review schema accurate and validated on an ongoing basis
Cap schema investment at the level the SEO fundamentals already justify
outputs: validation report (Rich Results Test or equivalent)

external_write.surface: site theme code / google tag manager

founder_sees: Confirmation of which pages now carry valid structured data, and which still need it.

name: Produce content clusters and buying guides
what: Build blog and guide content in buyer-intent formats that support a real money page, one cluster at a time, ahead of the season it targets.
encompasses: Build and optimize collection and product pages before writing any blog post
Only blog in buyer-intent formats that support a collection, not generic lifestyle posts
Build 1 cluster of 5 to 10 pieces around 1 money page before starting the next
Build and refresh seasonal category or guide pages ahead of the season, not after it starts
Map category content to the 5-stage customer-awareness ladder
Build the store's real content moat: testing notes, real customer photos, sizing data
Build a roundup or comparison page to break into a term owned by enterprise homepages
inputs: brand brain: testing notes and sizing data
founder_sees: A draft guide or cluster of posts around one money page, ready to review.

name: Produce comparison and alternatives pages
what: Write factual comparison and alternatives content that names competitors directly, since these are the formats both search and AI answers cite most for considered purchases.
encompasses: Write factual comparison and alternatives content that names competitors directly
Build the specific page formats AI answers actually cite: comparisons, buying guides, best-of roundups
Publish honest comparison pages against 3 to 4 bigger rivals
Cover a topic end to end but keep each intent on its own page type
Build comparison and trust content earlier for a high-AOV or considered-purchase store
founder_sees: A comparison page draft naming real competitors, with every claim checked against the brand record.

name: Run the content refresh, redirect and pruning program
what: Keep existing pages healthy: refresh stale or falling pages before writing anything new, handle discontinued and out-of-stock pages, and prune duplicate or cannibalizing content.
encompasses: Audit existing pages for wasted rankings and re-aim or fix them
Refresh a page-2-or-3 or CTR-falling page before writing anything new
Keep a ranking discontinued product page live with a shop-similar option instead of deleting it
Redirect a deleted product to its nearest relevant page, never an unrelated one
Run a periodic content refresh review across the whole site
Refresh high-intent pages every 2 months with real new facts
Refresh a sleeper page that already has links and traffic before writing a new one
Copy the structure that performs, never the copy, when scaling a page template
Retitle an existing category page for a best-of query instead of writing a new one
Treat an out-of-stock or discontinued page as a citation risk, not only a sales one
founder_sees: A prioritized list of what to refresh or redirect this month.

name: Run the internal linking program
what: Build and maintain internal links from content pages to money pages and back, fix orphan pages, and add navigational links on product and collection pages.
encompasses: Build hub-and-spoke internal links from body copy, not just the menu
Add an outbound citation and a money-page link to every content page
Add breadcrumbs, category tag links and a related-products module to product pages
Find and fix every orphan page with no internal link
Link from money pages out to the best-performing supporting articles
Link every guide, FAQ and comparison page to the product it sells for
founder_sees: A list of missing internal links, with the fix applied or proposed.

name: Run backlink, digital PR and mention outreach
what: Earn links and brand mentions through disclosed, relevant outreach: journalist queries, guest posts, broken-link and content-upgrade pitches, and review-site or listicle placements, in that priority order, never buying or swapping links.
encompasses: Never buy or swap links; disclose any sponsored placement with rel=sponsored
Point earned links at educational pages and the root domain, then pass authority inward
Screen every link prospect with a fixed checklist before any outreach
Sign up for journalist query platforms and answer relevant questions daily
Pitch guest posts and link inserts only with a real value offer, disclosed if paid
Run a backlink audit and disavow only with manual action or clear spam evidence
Prefer a link insertion, a stale-link pitch or a broken-link pitch over a new guest post
Build foundational entity links before guest posts or journalist outreach, then close the gap against competitors' backlink profile at a set monthly pace
Chase brand and product mentions before backlinks, aiming at review sites and gift guides first, then forums, then owned channels
Get onto the third-party listicles and Reddit threads AI engines already cite, participating as one named employee
Only pay for a placement the publisher itself labels sponsored or affiliate
Send a press release only for real news, and put the founder or a product expert on reporter platforms and relevant podcasts
inputs: brand brain: real news and expert credentials
founder_sees: A list of outreach targets and draft pitches, and a log of links and mentions earned.

name: Run local SEO and reputation program
what: For any brand with a physical location, run Google Business Profile, local citations and NAP consistency, plus the unincentivized review-collection program that feeds trust signals everywhere.
encompasses: Run a full Google Business Profile program for any store with a physical location
Build local citations and NAP consistency
Automate posting Instagram media to Google Business Profile photos
Turn each new blog post into a Google Business Profile update
Auto-reply to positive Google reviews only; route the rest to a human
Seed a Google Business Profile Q&A with a real customer question
Ask for reviews in person right after service, not only by automated text
Ask every buyer for an honest review, never pay, script or filter it
Spread review collection across more than one platform
Keep name, price and facts identical across site, feed and every marketplace listing
Keep platform brand information current for sales-channel sync
founder_sees: The local listing and review program status, with any negative review routed for a human reply.

name: Hand off marketplace and feed SEO readiness
what: Keep the merchant product feed accurate and complete so free Shopping listings, marketplace search and AI shopping surfaces read the brand correctly, and hand the actual listing work to Product and supply.
encompasses: List every eligible product in Google's free Shopping listings
List every eligible product on the marketplace that already owns the SERP or AI citations
Fix the Shopify global catalog and AI crawler access for AI shopping visibility
Keep the merchant feed accurate since shoppable AI cards read from it
Treat marketplace listings as a citation surface, not only a sales channel
Prepare product data fields for autonomous AI shopping agents
outputs: marketplace SEO handoff brief to Product and supply
founder_sees: A feed accuracy report and a handoff note to the product team for anything that needs a catalog fix.

name: Set up analytics and tag tracking
what: Install and keep current the no-code analytics stack: GA4, Search Console (domain property), and Tag Manager-based event tracking, without touching theme code.
encompasses: Install GA4 and Search Console before launch and keep them separate
Use a Search Console Domain property to cover every subdomain and protocol
Deploy analytics tags through Google Tag Manager, not direct code
Track add-to-cart and checkout clicks with Tag Manager, no dev code
Add social accounts as Search Console platform properties
founder_sees: Confirmation that GA4, Search Console and event tracking are installed and correctly scoped.

name: Report and diagnose SEO performance
what: Run the fixed-cadence Search Console and GA4 read, lead with organic revenue not vanity totals, and diagnose specific problems (CTR, traffic drops, device mismatch, bounce) from the data before touching a page.
encompasses: Report organic revenue and branded vs non-branded clicks every month, never raw traffic or vanity totals
Read leading indicators before clicks in the first months of a new SEO program
Push pages at positions 4 to 30 with impressions before writing anything new
Diagnose a high-impression, low-click page by position, and retarget its title/H1 to the query that earns its clicks
Diagnose a traffic drop by finding what the losing pages share
Track organic add-to-cart, checkout and purchase by landing page
Set a fixed cadence for keyword tracking, GSC and GA4 review, device/country splits, and bounce-rate triage on content pages
Do not build a custom dashboard until a free template or export stops being enough
Run the full technical, collection-page, product-page and keyword-map audits as recurring actions
Compare device traffic against device conversion every quarter, and diagnose wrong-audience targeting with three traffic signals
Investigate a small, high-engagement referral source as a partnership, and flag first-fold CTA or template A/B tests for the Site/CRO specialist
Cross-check an automated SEO tool's score against a second tool rather than comparing scores across vendors, and document technical gaps and a dated SEO baseline in the brand record
founder_sees: The monthly organic revenue number, non-branded clicks, and a short list of diagnosed problems with a fix each.

name: Vet SEO, link and AEO vendors before hiring
what: Screen any SEO agency, freelancer, link vendor or GEO/AEO vendor pitch for red flags before the founder signs anything, and treat every vendor statistic as a snapshot, not a fact.
encompasses: Screen every SEO pitch for red flags before hiring an agency, freelancer or tool
Ask for a named past client site and dates before hiring any link or SEO vendor
Set a 3-to-6-month organic revenue review window with the baseline recorded first
Ask a GEO vendor 5 questions and 3 probes before hiring them
Audit a vendor case study by keyword-difficulty band, and ask how it looks now
Track about 3 AI platforms and buy the cheapest tracker that does the job
Verify a vendor's claimed influence (for example on Reddit) before paying
Treat every AEO statistic in a vendor pitch as a snapshot, not a fact
founder_sees: A short scorecard on any SEO or AEO vendor pitch, with a clear recommend or reject.

name: Rewrite pages for answer-engine citation
what: Restructure and rewrite existing high-value pages so an AI answer engine can lift a direct, accurate answer: answer-first sections, atomic fact blocks, entity-rich sentences and buyer-phrased headlines.
encompasses: Answer every sub-question a buyer prompt fans into on one page
Open every page section with a direct answer under a question heading
Make each fact block on a page stand alone
Name the product and material; never say 'this item' or 'many users'
Write titles, H1s and openers in the shopper's own words
Build the page format that already wins the target prompt
Replace vague claims with real numbers, quotes and test data
Add one first-hand fact to every page before publishing
Write long buying guides 60% to 70% in short answer capsules
Give a proprietary material or method its own brand name
Rewrite one page end to end for AI citation, starting with the highest-traffic pages
inputs: brand brain: claims tiers and product facts
founder_sees: A rewritten version of the page built to be quoted accurately by an AI answer, with the facts it now leads with.

name: Build and maintain the brand facts page and fact consistency
what: Publish a facts page that answers every gap a prompt audit finds, and keep the same facts identical everywhere an engine can read them: site, schema, feed, directories, reviews.
encompasses: Publish a brand facts page that answers every gap the prompt audit found
Make every brand fact match everywhere an engine can read it
Keep facts identical across site, schema, feed, directories and reviews
founder_sees: A facts page draft and a report on where the brand's facts disagree across the web.

name: Correct wrong AI-stated facts about the brand
what: When an AI answer states something wrong about the brand, fix it at the source (the site) first, then the publisher it likely came from, then the wider web, in that order.
encompasses: Correct a wrong AI fact at the site first, then the publisher, then everywhere else
Run the end-to-end fact-correction workflow from a prompt audit to a fixed source
Recheck the corrected fact on the same engines a month later to confirm it held
founder_sees: A plan to fix a specific wrong AI fact, starting with the brand's own site.

name: Monitor AI visibility and report share of voice
what: Run the recurring audit of how ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI describe the brand: a frozen prompt set, a gap classification, and a monthly report on share of voice, citation persistence and channel quality, never a single AI rank number.
encompasses: List every brand entity before auditing AI visibility
Ask each AI engine what it knows about the brand, then open every source it cites, and check whether the answer came from live search or memory
Run a 6-gap AI visibility audit on the store and named competitors, and repeat it monthly with a deeper pass every quarter
Filter the tracker for mentioned-but-not-cited and others-only gaps, and fix the single biggest gap first
Report AI share of voice on a frozen prompt set run several times, never a single AI rank number
Split every mention report into named, cited and linked, and log every citation found to recheck for persistence
Never accept a raw AI citation or mention count as a win on its own
Measure AI visibility with 3 pillars together: referrals, bot logs and survey, tracking which pages citation bots actually fetch
Build a GA4 channel for AI-referred sessions, and ask 'how did you hear about us' with AI options listed first
Judge the AI channel by order conversion and AOV against organic every month, and verify citations directly rather than from crawler logs
Prove one AEO tactic with a control group before calling it a rule, and never treat an unproven tactic as settled fact
Set measurement to the brand's real primary market, break citations down by source type, and split AI-referred sessions by page type and customer status
founder_sees: A monthly report on how AI assistants describe the brand, whether it's improving, and what the single biggest gap is.
